Capability: Ability to adaptively change system response characteristics (output gain) in an experience-dependent manner by integrating multiple sensory/motor inputs (vestibular signals and visual error signals). Example of supervised cerebellar learning as formalized by Marr-Albus-Ito theory (Marr 1969; Albus 1971; Ito 1982).
Mechanism: High-dimensional sparse coding (R.Sensory-Context-Coding) expands the input space to make different vestibular stimuli discriminable. Error-dependent plasticity (R.Error-Dependent-Plasticity) updates PF-PC synaptic weights based on CF teaching signals. This two-stage processing changes PC firing patterns for specific head motion contexts, thereby adapting VOR output gain.
Requirements: Interface is ([U.MVN]) = R.VOR-Learning([U.MVN], [U.IO-DC]). The structure generating noROI output [U.MVN] from noROI inputs [U.MVN] and [U.IO-DC] is fully consistent with the Requirement. The interface satisfies the TLF requirement: (all noROI outputs) = R.TLF(all noROI inputs), confirming that MVN is correctly functioning as both input provider and output target.
Output Semantics: Receives [U.MVN] head velocity/eye velocity signals (Output Semantics: eye velocity command adapted to vestibular stimulation) via mossy fibers and [U.IO-DC] visual error signals (Output Semantics: teaching signal encoding retinal slip) via climbing fibers; adaptively modifies inhibitory control output to [U.MVN] (FTN) to optimize VOR gain. Input: [U.MVN] vestibular signal; [U.IO-DC] visual error signal. Output: modified inhibitory signal to [U.MVN] (FTN; expressed as adaptive change in VOR gain).
column12: Overall function to adaptively change VOR gain using visual error (retinal slip) as teaching signal. Integrates all ROI_Input to ROI_Output pathways.

Capability: Ability to non-linearly transform few convergent inputs (mossy fibers) into high-dimensional sparse distributed representation (parallel fibers) through expansion coding combined with feedback inhibition-based sparsification. Theoretically predicted by Marr (1969) and supported by anatomical evidence of GC-GoC circuit in Eccles et al. (1967).
Mechanism: GC receives input from 4-5 mossy fibers via dendritic claw structure. Many GCs receiving different combinations of MF inputs expand the original input space to far higher dimensions. GoC receives GC activity and direct MF input, applying GABAergic feedback inhibition to sparsify GC activity. Sparse coding results in near-orthogonal representation of different vestibular stimulus conditions on PFs, facilitating PC discrimination of sensory contexts.
Requirements Realization by Interface: Interface is ([U.PC], [U.BC], [U.SC]) = R.Sensory-Context-Coding([U.MVN]). Single external input [U.MVN] generates three external outputs [U.PC], [U.BC], [U.SC]. Internal loop of [U.GC] performing dimensional expansion and [U.GoC] maintaining sparseness via feedback inhibition realizes the high-dimensional sparse transformation. The structure converting single MF input into numerous PF outputs across PC, BC, and SC is consistent with the Interface.
Requirements: Receives head velocity/eye velocity signals from [U.MVN] (Output Semantics: eye velocity command corresponding to vestibular stimulation) via mossy fibers, and transforms them into high-dimensional sparse parallel fiber representation that [U.PC] can discriminate. Also generates parallel fiber signals for [U.BC] and [U.SC] providing basis for inhibitory modulation. Input: [U.MVN] head motion and eye velocity signals. Output: high-dimensional sparse pattern activity to [U.PC], [U.BC], [U.SC].
Comments: Converts vestibular/motor signals from MVN into high-dimensional sparse representation. GC performs dimensional expansion encoding; GoC maintains sparseness via feedback inhibition.

Capability: Delta rule-like supervised learning ability that updates synaptic weights based on coincident activity of teaching signal (climbing fiber) and context signal (parallel fiber). Based on cerebellar LTD/LTP mechanism formalized by Ito hypothesis (Ito 1982; Broussard et al. 2011; Lisberger 2021).
Mechanism: CF (from IO-DC) firing (complex spike) functions as error signal, inducing mGluR1-dependent LTD at simultaneously active PF-PC synapses. LTD reduces PC firing rate, relieving inhibition on MVN (FTN). SC (in R.CF-PF-Plasticity) modulates CF-PF integration efficiency at PC dendrites; BC (in R.Output-Timing-Control) sharpens PC firing timing. As learning progresses, feedback from CF automatically converges learning (Lisberger 2021 Principle 3).
Requirements Realization by Interface: Interface is ([U.MVN]) = R.Error-Dependent-Plasticity([U.GC], [U.IO-DC]). [U.GC] (PF context signal) and [U.IO-DC] (CF teaching signal) are the two external inputs generating [U.MVN] inhibitory output. Internally [U.PC] is the main site for CF-PF integration (R.CF-PF-Plasticity); [U.BC] (via R.Output-Timing-Control) and [U.SC] (via R.CF-PF-Plasticity) modulate it. The causal chain of error-dependent plasticity induction to output change is consistent with the Interface.
Requirements: Integrates [U.GC] high-dimensional sparse pattern activity (Output Semantics: sparse high-dimensional pattern activity encoding vestibular stimulation and eye movement context) and [U.IO-DC] visual error signal (Output Semantics: teaching signal encoding retinal slip) to induce PC synaptic plasticity and adaptively change inhibitory output to [U.MVN] (FTN). Input: [U.GC] sparse pattern activity; [U.IO-DC] teaching signal. Output: modified inhibition to [U.MVN].
Comments: Integrates climbing fiber teaching signals and parallel fiber context signals to induce synaptic plasticity; adaptively modifies inhibitory output to vestibular nucleus FTNs. PC is the primary site; SC and BC modulate the process.

Capability: Ability to induce long-term changes in synaptic strength (LTD/LTP) at specific synapses depending on coincident activity of teaching signal (CF) and context signal (PF). Realized by mGluR1-dependent LTD mechanism (Ito 1982; Broussard et al. 2011) and GABA-B-dependent LTP (Broussard et al. 2011; Schonewille et al. 2011).
Mechanism: At PC dendritic spines, coincident glutamate release from PF and strong depolarization from CF (complex spike) activates Ca2+ influx and mGluR1-PKCa pathway, leading to AMPA receptor phosphorylation and internalization (LTD). PF activity alone without CF firing induces the reverse LTP. SC inhibits outer PC dendritic shafts to modulate magnitude and selectivity of Ca2+ influx and thereby the LTD induction threshold.
Requirements Realization by Interface: Interface is ([U.MVN]) = R.CF-PF-Plasticity([U.GC], [U.IO-DC], [U.BC]). Three external inputs (PF signal from [U.GC], CF signal from [U.IO-DC], lateral inhibition from [U.BC]) generate [U.MVN] inhibitory output. [U.SC] internally modulates CF-PF integration at PC dendritic shafts, and this structure is consistent with the Requirement.
Requirements: Integrates [U.GC] parallel fiber activity (Output Semantics: sparse high-dimensional pattern activity) and [U.IO-DC] climbing fiber activity (Output Semantics: visual error teaching signal) at [U.PC] dendrites; induces LTD (gain-up learning via CF-PF coincident activity) or LTP (gain-down learning via PF-alone activity) to change inhibitory output to [U.MVN]. Lateral inhibition from [U.BC] also modifies the integration process. Input: [U.GC] PF signal; [U.IO-DC] CF signal; [U.BC] inhibitory signal. Output: modified inhibition to [U.MVN].
Comments: Detects CF-PF coincident activity at PC dendrites and induces LTD (gain-up learning) or LTP (gain-down learning). SC modulates CF-PF integration efficiency at outer PC dendrites near climbing fiber synaptic sites.

Capability: Ability to refine output neuron firing timing via lateral inhibition proportional to parallel fiber activity, achieving winner-take-all-like contrast enhancement. PC axon initial segment inhibition by BC pinceau structure is based on classical anatomical research of Eccles et al. (1967).
Mechanism: When parallel fibers excite BC, BC GABAergic axon terminals surround the PC axon initial segment (pinceau) applying powerful inhibition. This lateral inhibition selectively inhibits PCs that are about to fire, enhancing spatiotemporal contrast and allowing specific VOR learning-related PCs to send clear signals over other PCs, sharpening the inhibitory output delivered to MVN (FTN).
Requirements Realization by Interface: Interface is ([U.MVN]) = R.Output-Timing-Control([U.GC], [U.IO-DC], [U.SC]). Three external inputs [U.GC], [U.IO-DC], and [U.SC] generate [U.MVN] inhibitory output. [U.BC] inserts lateral somatic inhibition between GC and PC in an internal loop; PC output timing refinement via this pinceau inhibition is consistent with the Requirement.
Requirements: [U.BC] receiving [U.GC] parallel fiber activity (Output Semantics: sparse high-dimensional pattern activity) sends lateral inhibition to [U.PC] axon initial segment (pinceau), refining PC firing timing and magnitude to maximize contrast of inhibitory output to [U.MVN] (FTN). Modulation from [U.IO-DC] and [U.SC] is also combined to determine the integrated PC output. Input: [U.GC] PF signal; [U.IO-DC] CF signal; [U.SC] dendritic inhibition signal. Output: temporally refined inhibition to [U.MVN].
Comments: BC receives parallel fiber signals from GC and delivers lateral inhibition to PC axon initial segment (pinceau); refines PC firing timing and magnitude to optimize inhibitory output to MVN (FTN). PC and BC together constitute somatic-level output control.

Capability: Expansion coding ability: non-linearly transforms sparse convergent inputs (mossy fibers from a few inputs per GC) into a high-dimensional sparse output representation (parallel fibers) encoding diverse contextual information. Predicted by Marr-Albus theory (Marr 1969; Albus 1971); supported in the VOR learning context by Lisberger (2021).
Mechanism: Each GC receives 4-5 mossy fiber inputs via dendritic claws. Large numbers of GCs each receiving distinct MF input combinations achieve high-dimensional expansion of the original input space. GoC inhibition (feedback and feedforward) limits the number of simultaneously active GCs, realizing sparse coding. As a result, parallel fibers provide a near-orthogonal high-dimensional feature representation of the original input signals.
Implementation of Uniform Circuit: [U.GC] = sigma(W_MF * [U.MVN] - [U.GoC]); where sigma is firing threshold function and W_MF is mossy fiber synaptic weight matrix (GC x input fiber dimensions)
Requirements Realization by Interface: Interface is ([U.PC], [U.GoC], [U.BC], [U.SC]) = GC([U.MVN], [U.GoC]). [U.MVN] is the primary input and [U.GoC] is the inhibitory modulatory input; outputs are sent to [U.PC], [U.GoC], [U.BC], [U.SC]. The Requirement for high-dimensional sparse transformation via expansion coding followed by GoC sparsification is consistent with this Interface.
Requirements: Receives [U.MVN] head velocity signal and [U.GoC] inhibitory feedback; transforms them into high-dimensional sparse representation deliverable to [U.PC] as parallel fiber signals required for learning. Input: [U.MVN] head velocity signal; [U.GoC] inhibitory feedback. Output: sparse high-dimensional pattern activity to [U.PC].
Output Semantics: [GC] Sparse high-dimensional pattern activity encoding vestibular stimulation and eye movement context (decorrelated representation on parallel fibers)
Comments: Located in granule cell layer of cerebellar cortex. Most numerous neurons in brain. Performs expansion coding from mossy fiber input to parallel fiber output. Critical for VOR learning context coding. ROI-internal.

Capability: Supervised learning ability: updates parallel fiber-Purkinje cell synaptic weights using climbing fiber input as teaching signal (LTD/LTP). Formalized in Ito hypothesis (Ito 1972; Ito 1982); directly supported by in vitro and in vivo plasticity experiments (Broussard et al. 2011; Schonewille et al. 2011; Lisberger 2021).
Mechanism: Under normal conditions PC fires simple spikes at high frequency (~70 Hz), tonically inhibiting FTN in MVN. During gain-up learning: coincident PF and CF activity triggers mGluR1 signaling pathway and Ca2+ influx, inducing LTD at active PF-PC synapses (AMPA receptor internalization). Post-learning reduction in PC simple spike rate relieves MVN FTN from inhibition, increasing VOR gain. During gain-down learning: PF activity without CF induces LTP, increasing PC firing and reducing VOR gain.
Implementation of Uniform Circuit: W_PF(t+1) = W_PF(t) - eta_LTD * [U.GC] * [U.IO-DC] + eta_LTP * [U.GC] * (1 - [U.IO-DC]); [U.PC] = W_PF * [U.GC] - [U.BC] - [U.SC]; where W_PF is PF-PC synaptic weight vector; eta_LTD and eta_LTP are learning rates
Requirements Realization by Interface: Interface is ([U.MVN]) = PC([U.GC], [U.IO-DC], [U.BC], [U.SC]). [U.GC] (parallel fibers), [U.IO-DC] (climbing fibers), [U.BC] (somatic inhibition), and [U.SC] (dendritic inhibition) are the four inputs converging to generate [U.MVN] inhibitory output. The causal chain of CF error signal triggering LTD at PF-PC synapse and thereby changing MVN inhibition is fully consistent with the Interface.
Requirements: Integrates [U.GC] high-dimensional context signals, [U.IO-DC] CF teaching signals, and inhibitory inputs from [U.BC] and [U.SC]; uses CF activity as error signal to induce LTD/LTP at PF-PC synapses, plastically changing inhibitory output to [U.MVN] (FTN) to optimize VOR gain. Input: [U.GC] PF signal; [U.IO-DC] CF signal; [U.BC] somatic inhibition; [U.SC] dendritic inhibition. Output: modified inhibitory signal to [U.MVN].
Output Semantics: [PC] Plastically modified vestibular stimulus response (inhibitory output strength modified by learning to represent adapted VOR gain)
Comments: Sole output neuron of cerebellar cortex. Primary site of LTD/LTP plasticity for VOR learning. Integrates ~100,000 PF synapses and 1 CF per cell. ROI-internal.

Capability: Ability to generate feedback inhibition proportional to sensory/motor input intensity, sparsifying and normalizing downstream neuron (GC) output. Sparseness maintenance is a central premise of Marr-Albus theory (Eccles et al. 1967).
Mechanism: GC excites GoC via parallel fibers and MF directly excites GoC; GoC then synapses via GABA-ergic axons onto GC dendritic claws at cerebellar glomeruli (glomerular structure). This inhibition limits the number of simultaneously active GCs, maintaining sparse representation. Both feedback (after GC fires) and feedforward (from MF) inhibition contribute to sparsification.
Implementation of Uniform Circuit: [U.GoC] = g([U.GC], [U.MVN]) = alpha * [U.MVN] + beta * [U.GC]; where alpha and beta are positive coefficients
Requirements Realization by Interface: Interface is ([U.GC]) = GoC([U.GC], [U.MVN]). GC and MVN are inputs; GC is the output target. GC-GoC feedback loop combined with MVN feedforward input maintains sparse coding of GC activity, consistent with the Requirement.
Requirements: Receives [U.GC] parallel fiber activity and [U.MVN] mossy fiber activity; sends inhibitory feedback to [U.GC] to maintain sparse coding of granule cell layer, preventing excessive GC activity that would degrade PC discrimination of VOR stimuli. Input: [U.GC] parallel fiber activity; [U.MVN] mossy fiber activity. Output: inhibitory feedback regulating [U.GC] excitability.
Output Semantics: [GoC] Amount of inhibitory feedback on granule cells proportional to parallel fiber and mossy fiber input strength
Comments: Located in granule cell layer. Largest inhibitory interneuron in cerebellum. Provides feedback and feedforward inhibition to GC via GABA/glycinergic synapses at cerebellar glomeruli. Maintains sparseness of GC activity. ROI-internal.

Capability: Ability to control spike generation of output neurons (Purkinje cells) through lateral inhibition proportional to parallel fiber activity, implementing winner-take-all-like contrast enhancement (Eccles et al. 1967).
Mechanism: Parallel fibers excite BC, which then forms GABA-ergic axon terminals (basket structure) surrounding PC axon initial segment (pinceau), inhibiting action potential generation. This lateral inhibition selectively suppresses PCs receiving strong PF input from less active GCs, enhancing the contrast between active and inactive PCs and sharpening the temporal precision of PC output.
Implementation of Uniform Circuit: [U.BC] = h([U.GC]) = gamma * [U.GC]; where gamma is a positive coefficient dependent on GC number and connection strength
Requirements Realization by Interface: Interface is ([U.PC]) = BC([U.GC]). GC parallel fiber input activates BC, which sends somatic lateral inhibition to PC. The feedforward inhibitory circuit GC->BC->PC that controls PC output timing is consistent with the Requirement.
Requirements: Receives [U.GC] parallel fiber activity and delivers lateral somatic inhibition to [U.PC] to sharpen PC firing timing, thereby refining the precision of VOR learning-related inhibitory signals from PC to MVN (FTN). Input: [U.GC] parallel fiber activity. Output: inhibitory signal to [U.PC] soma and axon initial segment.
Output Semantics: [BC] Inhibitory signal to PC soma based on parallel fiber activity (temporal sharpening of PC spike generation)
Comments: Located in inner molecular layer. Inhibitory interneuron providing lateral inhibition to PC soma and axon initial segment via pinceau structure. Controls PC output timing and magnitude. ROI-internal.

Capability: Ability to modulate the integration characteristics of PC dendrites (CF-PF coincidence detection) through inhibition of PC dendritic shafts proportional to parallel fiber activity (Eccles et al. 1967).
Mechanism: Parallel fibers excite SC, which then synapses via GABA-ergic axons onto outer PC dendritic shafts. Proximity to climbing fiber synaptic sites on PC dendrites allows SC inhibition to modulate magnitude and timing of Ca2+ influx triggered by CF firing, thereby adjusting LTD induction threshold and efficiency.
Implementation of Uniform Circuit: [U.SC] = k([U.GC]) = delta * [U.GC]; where delta is a positive coefficient
Requirements Realization by Interface: Interface is ([U.PC]) = SC([U.GC]). GC parallel fiber input activates SC, which sends dendritic inhibition to PC. The feedforward inhibitory circuit GC->SC->PC that modulates CF-PF integration at PC dendrites is consistent with the Requirement.
Requirements: Receives [U.GC] parallel fiber activity and delivers inhibition to [U.PC] outer dendrites to modulate CF-PF coincidence detection and thereby regulate LTD/LTP induction efficiency, contributing to proper adaptation of VOR gain. Input: [U.GC] parallel fiber activity. Output: inhibitory signal to [U.PC] outer dendritic shafts.
Output Semantics: [SC] Inhibitory signal to PC outer dendrites based on parallel fiber activity (modulation of CF-PF integration amount)
Comments: Located in outer molecular layer. Inhibitory interneuron providing inhibition to PC outer dendritic shafts. Located near climbing fiber synaptic sites; modulates CF-PF integration. ROI-internal.
